verses.text: The tribes of Reuben and Gad had very large herds and flocks. They saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were good places for animals.
So the people of Gad and Reuben came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community, and said,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
the land the LORD conquered for the community of Israel, is good land for animals, and we, your servants, have many animals."
They said, "If you are pleased with us, let this land be given to us, your servants, as our own. Do not make us cross the Jordan River."
Moses said to the people of Gad and Reuben, "Should your fellow Israelites go to war while you sit here?
Why are you trying to discourage the people of Israel from crossing over into the land the LORD has given them?
That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look at the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and then they discouraged the people of Israel from going into the land the LORD had given them.
The LORD was angry that day, and he made this promise:
'Because they did not follow me with all their hearts, not one of the men twenty years old or more who came out of Egypt will see the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Only Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun will see it, because they followed the LORD with all their hearts.'
The LORD was angry with Israel, and he made them wander in the desert for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in his sight had died.
And now here you are, a new brood of sinners, taking your fathers' place and making the LORD even angrier with Israel!
If you turn away from following him, he will leave all these people in the desert again, and you will be the cause of their destruction."
Then they came up to Moses and said, "We want to build pens here for our animals and towns for our children.

But we ourselves will arm ourselves and lead the people of Israel into battle until we have brought them to their own land. Meanwhile our children will live in towns with strong walls, safe from the people of the land.
We will not come back to our homes until every Israelite has received his own land.
We will not take any land with them on the other side of the Jordan, because we have received our land here on the east side of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you will do this, if you will arm yourselves for battle before the LORD,
and all your armed men cross the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies ahead of him,
and the land is conquered before the LORD, then you may come back. You will have done your duty to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be yours before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you will be sinning against the LORD, and you can be sure your sin will catch up with you.
Build towns for your children and pens for your sheep, but do what you have promised."
The people of Gad and Reuben said to Moses, "We, your servants, will do as you, our master, command.
Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our animals will stay here in the towns of Gilead.
But all of us, your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over to fight before the LORD, just as you, our master, have said."
So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family leaders of the tribes of Israel.

He said to them, "If the people of Gad and Reuben, every man armed for battle, cross the Jordan with you before the LORD, and the land is conquered for you, then give them the land of Gilead as their own.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must take their share of land with you in Canaan."
The people of Gad and Reuben answered, "We, your servants, will do what the LORD has said.
We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the land we own will be on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave the people of Gad and Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan. He gave them the whole land with its towns and the land around them.
The people of Gad rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth Nimrah, and Beth Haran as towns with strong walls, and they built pens for their sheep.
The people of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, and Baal Meon, whose names were changed, and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they rebuilt.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
So Moses gave Gilead to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, and they settled there.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, captured some villages and called them Havvoth Jair, which means villages of Jair.
Nobah captured Kenath and the villages around it, and called it Nobah after his own name.
